Available tools: rhobs_metrics, rhobs_logs, rhobs_alerts

docs.title: Operations Reference
docs.text: Quick-reference commands for day-to-day HCP operations. This page assumes you have oc authenticated to the Management Cluster.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these once per session:

# The environment: staging, production
export ENV=production

# The cluster ID (from OCM)
export CLUSTER_ID=abc123def456

# The cluster name (from OCM)
export CLUSTER_NAME=my-hcp-cluster

# Derived namespace variables
export HC_NS="ocm-${ENV}-${CLUSTER_ID}"
export HCP_NS="ocm-${ENV}-${CLUSTER_ID}-${CLUSTER_NAME}"

# The Management Cluster (from OCM describe)
export MC_NAME=$(ocm describe cluster $CLUSTER_ID | grep "Management Cluster" | awk '{print $NF}')

docs.title: Cluster Discovery
docs.text:
# Find Service Cluster for a region
ocm list clusters -p "search=name like 'hs-sc-%' and region.id='us-east-1'"

# Find Management Cluster for a specific hosted cluster
ocm describe cluster $CLUSTER_ID | grep -i "management cluster"

# List all hosted clusters on a given MC
ocm list clusters \
  -p "hypershift.management_cluster LIKE '${MC_NAME}'" \
  --columns id,name,state,version

# List all MCs managed by an SC
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters \
  -p search="parent.cluster_id='$SC_CLUSTER_ID'"

docs.title: HostedCluster Status
docs.text:
# Quick health check
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME

# Detailed conditions
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}' | jq '.'

# Check availability
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Available")].status}'

# Check all NodePools
oc get nodepool -n $HC_NS

# Check NodePool details
oc get nodepool -n $HC_NS -o wide

docs.title: Control Plane Health
docs.text:
# List all pods in the HCP namespace
oc get pods -n $HCP_NS

# Check for any non-Running pods
oc get pods -n $HCP_NS | grep -v Running | grep -v Completed

# Control plane operator (the reconciler — start here for most issues)
oc logs -n $HCP_NS deploy/control-plane-operator -f

# kube-apiserver
oc logs -n $HCP_NS -l app=kube-apiserver

# etcd health
oc exec -n $HCP_NS etcd-0 -- \
  etcdctl endpoint health \
  --cacert=/etc/etcd/tls/etcd-ca/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/etcd/tls/client/etcd-client.crt \
  --key=/etc/etcd/tls/client/etcd-client.key \
  --endpoints=https://etcd-client:2379

# etcd leader status
oc exec -n $HCP_NS etcd-0 -- \
  etcdctl endpoint status \
  --cacert=/etc/etcd/tls/etcd-ca/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/etcd/tls/client/etcd-client.crt \
  --key=/etc/etcd/tls/client/etcd-client.key \
  --endpoints=https://etcd-client:2379 -w table

# capi-provider (for worker provisioning issues)
oc logs -n $HCP_NS deploy/capi-provider

docs.title: Worker Nodes
docs.text:
# List all machines (worker CRs on MC, not in the hosted cluster)
oc get machines -n $HCP_NS

# List AWSMachines
oc get awsmachines -n $HCP_NS

# Check machine status
oc describe machine -n $HCP_NS $MACHINE_NAME

# Pending CSRs (new node joining)
# Run this against the HOSTED cluster, not the MC
oc get csr --kubeconfig $KUBECONFIG_HOSTED | grep Pending

# Approve a CSR manually (if machine-approver is stuck)
oc adm certificate approve $CSR_NAME --kubeconfig $KUBECONFIG_HOSTED

docs.title: Normal: Admin Kubeconfig
docs.text:
# Extract admin kubeconfig
oc get secret -n $HC_NS ${CLUSTER_NAME}-admin-kubeconfig \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.kubeconfig}' | base64 -d > /tmp/hcp-kubeconfig

# Use it
oc --kubeconfig /tmp/hcp-kubeconfig get nodes

docs.title: Emergency: SSM + crictl (when API is down)
docs.text:
# Find an EC2 instance ID for a worker node
aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=*${CLUSTER_NAME}*" \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,State.Name,PrivateIpAddress]' \
  --output table

# Start SSM session
aws ssm start-session --target $INSTANCE_ID

# On the node: check kubelet
sudo systemctl status kubelet

# On the node: check containers
sudo crictl ps

# On the node: check logs
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f

docs.title: OCM-Down: apply-bootstrap container
docs.text:
# If OCM is unavailable but the MC is accessible
oc exec -n $HCP_NS $KAS_POD -c apply-bootstrap -- \
  oc --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/admin-kubeconfig get nodes

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
# Check PrivateLink endpoint service status
oc get awsendpointservice -n $HCP_NS
oc describe awsendpointservice -n $HCP_NS

# Check konnectivity tunnel
oc logs -n $HCP_NS deploy/konnectivity-server | tail -50

# Check VPC endpoint in customer account
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints \
  --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=*${CLUSTER_NAME}*"

docs.title: Alerts and Monitoring
docs.text:
# Check if cluster alerts are suppressed
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.hypershift\.openshift\.io/disable-cluster-alerts}'

# Suppress alerts (during maintenance)
oc annotate hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  hypershift.openshift.io/disable-cluster-alerts=true

# Remove alert suppression
oc annotate hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  hypershift.openshift.io/disable-cluster-alerts-

# Check MonitoringStack health
oc get monitoringstack -n $HCP_NS

docs.title: Maintenance Mode (SC/MC)
docs.text:
Maintenance mode affects ALL clusters on the MC

Placing an MC in maintenance mode affects every HCP on that MC.

# Check current maintenance state
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters/$MC_ID

# Enable maintenance (via Fleet Manager API, SRE use only)
# This pauses HyperShift Operator reconciliation

# Check which clusters are affected
ocm list clusters \
  -p "hypershift.management_cluster LIKE '$MC_NAME'" \
  --columns id,name,state

docs.title: Cluster Lifecycle Commands
docs.text:
# Create a cluster (staging)
rosa create cluster \
  --hosted-cp \
  --cluster-name $CLUSTER_NAME \
  --sts \
  --mode auto \
  --region us-east-2 \
  --subnet-ids $SUBNET_IDS \
  --oidc-config-id $OIDC_ID

# Delete a cluster
rosa delete cluster -c $CLUSTER_NAME --yes

# Clean up OIDC (after deletion)
rosa delete oidc-config --oidc-config-id $OIDC_ID

# Upgrade control plane
rosa upgrade cluster -c $CLUSTER_NAME --version 4.16.5

# Upgrade workers (NodePool)
rosa upgrade machinepool -c $CLUSTER_NAME \
  --machinepool workers \
  --version 4.16.5

docs.title: Useful One-Liners
docs.text:
# Count HCPs per MC in a region
ocm list clusters \
  -p "region.id='us-east-1' and name like 'hs-mc-%'" \
  --columns name,id | while read MC_NAME MC_ID; do
  COUNT=$(ocm list clusters \
    -p "hypershift.management_cluster LIKE '$MC_NAME'" \
    --count-only 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$MC_NAME: $COUNT HCPs"
done

# Find all degraded HCPs in a region
ocm list clusters \
  -p "region.id='us-east-1' and state='Error'" \
  --columns id,name,state,version

# Get the admin kubeconfig for a cluster and export it
oc get secret -n $HC_NS ${CLUSTER_NAME}-admin-kubeconfig \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.kubeconfig}' \
  | base64 -d \
  | KUBECONFIG=/dev/stdin oc get nodes

# Watch all pods in HCP namespace coming up
watch -n 5 "oc get pods -n $HCP_NS | sort -k3"

docs.title: Recovery & Disaster Recovery
docs.text: ROSA HCP uses OADP (OpenShift API for Data Protection) and Velero for automated backups and recovery. This page covers what's backed up, what's not, and how to restore.

docs.title: What is (and isn't) Backed Up
docs.text: Component Location Backed Up? Recovery Method Cluster record OCM Database ✓ (DB backups) DB restore ManifestWork Service Cluster ✗ NOT backed up Manual recreation HostedCluster CR Management Cluster ✓ Velero restore HostedControlPlane CR Control Plane Namespace ✓ Velero restore etcd StatefulSet + PVCs Control Plane Namespace ✓ (CSI snapshots) Velero restore Control Plane Pods Control Plane Namespace ✓ Velero restore NodePool CR Management Cluster ✓ CAPI self-healing or Velero Worker EC2 Instances AWS ✗ NOT backed up Reprovisioned via NodePool

docs.title: ManifestWork Structure (5 per cluster)
docs.text:
ManifestWork Contents Delete During Recovery? ${CLUSTER_ID} Main resources (HostedCluster, NodePool) Yes ${CLUSTER_ID}-00-namespaces Namespace definitions Yes ${CLUSTER_ID}-workers Worker node configuration Yes ${CLUSTER_ID}-00-dr BackupStorageLocation + Schedule NO — Velero depends on this ${CLUSTER_ID}-01-dr DR credentials Secret NO — Velero depends on this

Critical

The -00-dr ManifestWork manages the BackupStorageLocation (BSL). If deleted, Velero cannot locate backups.

docs.title: DR Scenario Coverage
docs.text: Scenario Recoverable? Accidental deletion of HCP in MC ✓ Full Broken HCP (etcd corruption) ✓ Full Partial deletion of HCP resources in MC ✓ Auto-heals ocm delete <cluster> (customer-initiated) ✗ Not recoverable Accidental deletion of HCP record in OCM DB ✗ Not recoverable Accidental deletion of ManifestWorks on SC ✗ (can restore in detached mode only) Full SC loss ✗ (can restore HCPs in detached mode) Full MC loss ✗ Not recoverable

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
export CLUSTER_ID="<cluster-id>"
export DOMAIN_PREFIX="<cluster-domain-prefix>"
export CLUSTER_ENV="<int|stage|prod>"
export JIRA_TICKET="<OHSS-XXXXX>"
export HC_NAMESPACE="ocm-${CLUSTER_ENV}-${CLUSTER_ID}"
export HCP_NAMESPACE="ocm-${CLUSTER_ENV}-${CLUSTER_ID}-${DOMAIN_PREFIX}"

docs.title: Assess the Failure
docs.text:
ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --manager

# Check HostedCluster
oc get hostedcluster ${DOMAIN_PREFIX} -n ${HC_NAMESPACE}

# Check namespace exists
oc get namespace ${HCP_NAMESPACE}

# Count control plane pods
oc get pods -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} --no-headers | wc -l
Symptom Recovery Type HostedCluster missing or has deletionTimestamp Full Restore Namespace missing or Terminating Full Restore HC exists but corrupted, control plane functional Partial Restore etcd pods CrashLooping, volume data lost Full Restore Only ManifestWorks deleted (SC issue) ManifestWork-Only Restore

docs.title: Full Restore (Automated)
docs.text:
The full restore procedure is automated by restore-hcp.sh:

# 1. Generate kubeconfigs
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/mc.kubeconfig ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --manager
KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sc.kubeconfig ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --service

# 2. Embed elevation
for kc in /tmp/mc.kubeconfig /tmp/sc.kubeconfig; do
  yq -i '.users[0].user.as = "backplane-cluster-admin"' "${kc}"
done

# 3. Run restore script
./restore-hcp.sh --cluster-id ${CLUSTER_ID} \
  --mc-kubeconfig /tmp/mc.kubeconfig \
  --sc-kubeconfig /tmp/sc.kubeconfig

docs.title: What the Script Does (in order)
docs.text:
1. Back up all ManifestWorks from the Service Cluster
  2. Verify Velero backup and BackupStorageLocation
  3. Disable ManifestWork reconciliation (patch to ReadOnly)
  4. Delete HCP resources on MC (webhooks, NodePools, HostedCluster)
  5. Wait for resource teardown and namespace deletion
  6. Create Velero restore from selected backup
  7. Wait for restore completion
  8. Restore ManifestWork reconciliation
  9. Verify recovery (HostedCluster, pods, etcd, PVCs)
  10. Clean up workspace (contains sensitive backup data)

docs.title: Post-Restore Notes
docs.text:
etcd stuck on startup: 

ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  annotate hostedcluster ${DOMAIN_PREFIX} -n ${HC_NAMESPACE} \
  hypershift.openshift.io/restart-date=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
Allow ~30 minutes to stabilize (tracked in OCPBUGS-76772).

Backplane access delay: Even after CP is healthy, SRE backplane access may take ~30 minutes to restore (VPCE re-establishment). Customer access is NOT affected.

# Track VPCE readiness
oc get vpce -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE}

docs.title: ManifestWork-Only Restore
docs.text:
When only ManifestWorks were deleted but etcd/PVCs are intact:

ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --service

# Restore all ManifestWorks from backup
for mw_file in ~/backup/${CLUSTER_ID}/service-cluster/*.yaml; do
  ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- apply -f ${mw_file}
done

# Wait ~10-15 minutes for ACM to reconcile
rosa describe cluster -c ${DOMAIN_PREFIX} | grep State

# Clean up backup (contains sensitive customer data)
[ -n "${CLUSTER_ID}" ] && rm -rf ~/backup/"${CLUSTER_ID}"/

docs.title: Partial Restore (HostedCluster CR Only)
docs.text:
When CR is corrupted but pods are still running:

ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --manager

# List available backups
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n openshift-adp exec deployment/velero -c velero -- \
  ./velero backup get | grep ${CLUSTER_ID}

# Create restore
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n openshift-adp exec deployment/velero -c velero -- \
  ./velero restore create --from-backup <backup-name>

# Check status
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n openshift-adp exec deployment/velero -c velero -- \
  ./velero restore describe <restore-name>

docs.title: Velero Backup (Management Cluster)
docs.text:
ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --manager

# Find the schedule
oc get schedule -n openshift-adp | grep "${CLUSTER_ID}"

# Trigger backup
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n openshift-adp exec deployment/velero -c velero -- \
  ./velero backup create --from-schedule ${CLUSTER_ID}-daily

# Verify completion
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n openshift-adp exec deployment/velero -c velero -- \
  ./velero backup get | grep ${CLUSTER_ID}

docs.title: Proactive ManifestWork Backup (Service Cluster)
docs.text:
ManifestWorks are not automatically backed up. Do this proactively:

mkdir -p ~/backup/${CLUSTER_ID}/service-cluster
ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --service
export MC_NAME="<mc-namespace-from-login>"

# Backup all ManifestWorks for this cluster
for mw in $(ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  get manifestwork -n ${MC_NAME} -l api.openshift.com/id=${CLUSTER_ID} \
  --no-headers | awk '{print $1}'); do
  ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
    get manifestwork ${mw} -n ${MC_NAME} -o yaml \
    > ~/backup/${CLUSTER_ID}/service-cluster/${mw}.yaml
done

docs.title: Restoring Deleted ClusterRoles
docs.text:
If all or most ClusterRoles are accidentally deleted, the cluster cannot function.

Symptoms: - Users receive Forbidden errors for all API operations - Error: clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "cluster-admin" not found - Operators degrading rapidly

docs.title: Option 1: Restart the KAS Pod (fastest)
docs.text:
The KAS rbac/bootstrap-roles PostStartHook recreates ~100 default Kubernetes ClusterRoles on every startup:

ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID} --manager
ocm backplane elevate "$REASON" -- \
  delete pods -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} -l app=kube-apiserver

After restart, self-healing chain: 1. KAS restart restores cluster-admin + ~100 default Kubernetes ClusterRoles 2. HCCO regains permissions, reconciles its managed ClusterRoles 3. ManifestWorks reconcile SRE/managed ClusterRoles (dedicated-admins-*, osd-*, backplane-*)

docs.title: Option 2: Manually Restore from a Healthy Cluster
docs.text:
# Get localhost-kubeconfig (bypasses RBAC entirely — system:masters)
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  get secrets localhost-kubeconfig -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.kubeconfig}' | base64 -d > /tmp/localhost-kubeconfig.yaml

# Check affected cluster version
oc get hostedclusters ${DOMAIN_PREFIX} -n ${HC_NAMESPACE} \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.version.history[0].version}'

# Export from a HEALTHY cluster at the SAME version
ocm backplane login <healthy-cluster-id>
oc get clusterroles -o yaml > /tmp/all-clusterroles.yaml

# Copy files into the KAS pod
KAS_POD=$(oc get pods -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} -l app=kube-apiserver \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')

ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  cp /tmp/localhost-kubeconfig.yaml \
  -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} ${KAS_POD}:/tmp/kubeconfig -c kube-apiserver

ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  cp /tmp/all-clusterroles.yaml \
  -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} ${KAS_POD}:/tmp/all-clusterroles.yaml -c kube-apiserver

# Apply ClusterRoles via localhost-kubeconfig
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} exec ${KAS_POD} -c kube-apiserver -- \
  /tmp/oc apply --kubeconfig=/tmp/kubeconfig -f /tmp/all-clusterroles.yaml

# Restart KAS to trigger bootstrap hook and clean up container changes
ocm backplane elevate '${JIRA_TICKET}' -- \
  delete pods -n ${HCP_NAMESPACE} -l app=kube-apiserver

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
# On the guest cluster
ocm backplane login ${CLUSTER_ID}
oc get clusterrole cluster-admin
oc get clusterroles --no-headers | wc -l  # Should be ~295
oc get clusteroperators

docs.title: Node Scheduling & Sizing
docs.text: HCP clusters don't run on generic nodes — they run on nodes selected specifically for the memory requirements of the control plane they're hosting. This page explains how that selection works.

docs.title: Why Dedicated Request-Serving Nodes?
docs.text:
In Classic ROSA, kube-apiserver runs on a dedicated master node (one of three). In HCP, multiple control planes share a Management Cluster, and each HCP's kube-apiserver runs as pods. Without dedicated nodes, kube-apiserver pods from different clusters would compete for the same CPU/memory, and a large or busy HCP could starve smaller ones.

The solution is request-serving nodes: dedicated pairs of nodes, one per HCP, that exclusively serve that HCP's kube-apiserver pods.

graph TD
    subgraph MC["Management Cluster"]
        subgraph RS1["Request-Serving Node Pair\n(cluster-1)"]
            KAS1a["kube-apiserver\ncluster-1 (pod 1)"]
            KAS1b["kube-apiserver\ncluster-1 (pod 2)"]
        end

        subgraph RS2["Request-Serving Node Pair\n(cluster-2)"]
            KAS2a["kube-apiserver\ncluster-2 (pod 1)"]
            KAS2b["kube-apiserver\ncluster-2 (pod 2)"]
        end

        subgraph NS1["Worker Nodes (general)"]
            ETCD["etcd pods\n(all clusters)"]
            CPO["control-plane-operator\n(all clusters)"]
            CAPI["capi-provider\n(all clusters)"]
        end
    end

    style RS1 fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#e65100
    style RS2 fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style NS1 fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0

Request-serving nodes are: - Deployed in pairs across 2 AZs (for HA) - Tainted with hypershift.openshift.io/request-serving-component: "true" so only HCP pods schedule there - Labeled with the cluster ID so anti-affinity rules pin pods to the right pair

docs.title: T-Shirt Sizing: Memory-Based Scaling
docs.text:
The size of the request-serving nodes is determined by the memory requirements of the control plane pods. This is called "t-shirt sizing" — clusters are bucketed into sizes based on observed memory usage.

graph LR
    SIZE["ClusterSizingConfiguration CR\n(hypershift-operator namespace)"]

    SIZE --> S["small\n< 350MB RAM\nm5.xlarge nodes"]
    SIZE --> M["medium\n350MB - 1750MB\nm5.2xlarge nodes"]
    SIZE --> L["large\n1750MB - 3500MB\nm5.4xlarge nodes"]
    SIZE --> XL["extra-large\n3500MB - 7000MB\nr5.4xlarge nodes"]
    SIZE --> XXL["extra-extra-large\n> 7000MB\nr5.8xlarge nodes"]

    style S fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style M fill:#fff9c4,stroke:#f57f17
    style L fill:#ffe0b2,stroke:#e65100
    style XL fill:#ffcdd2,stroke:#c62828
    style XXL fill:#f3e5f5,stroke:#7b1fa2

docs.title: How Sizing is Calculated
docs.text:
The HyperShift Operator samples the control plane pod memory every few minutes and updates the HostedCluster.Status.OAuthCallbackURLTemplate with the computed size class.

# View the sizing configuration
oc get clustersizingconfiguration -n hypershift-operator cluster -o yaml

# See what size a cluster is currently assigned
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME -o jsonpath='{.status.platform.aws.requestServingNodeType}'

docs.title: The Placeholder System: Fast Provisioning
docs.text:
Node provisioning takes time (~3–5 minutes for EC2 + bootstrap). If every new HCP had to wait for fresh nodes to provision, cluster creation would be very slow.

Placeholders solve this by maintaining a pool of warm, pre-provisioned request-serving nodes that are available immediately when a new HCP is created.

sequenceDiagram
    participant FM as Fleet Manager
    participant MC as Management Cluster
    participant PLACEHOLDER as Placeholder NodePool
    participant AWS as Customer AWS

    Note over FM,PLACEHOLDER: Idle time — placeholder pool maintained
    FM->>PLACEHOLDER: Ensure N placeholder node pairs exist
    PLACEHOLDER->>AWS: Provision EC2 nodes (pre-warm)
    AWS-->>PLACEHOLDER: Nodes ready, idle

    Note over FM,AWS: Cluster creation requested
    FM->>MC: Create HostedCluster
    MC->>PLACEHOLDER: Claim a placeholder pair (reassign labels)
    Note over MC: Node pair immediately available!
    MC-->>FM: Control plane scheduled in seconds

    Note over FM,PLACEHOLDER: Replenishment
    FM->>PLACEHOLDER: Create new placeholder to replace claimed one
    PLACEHOLDER->>AWS: Provision replacement EC2 node

Placeholder ConfigMap

The number of placeholder pairs per size class is controlled by a ConfigMap. Fleet Manager adjusts this based on regional demand patterns.

docs.title: How Pods Find Their Nodes
docs.text: Scheduling is enforced through a combination of node selectors, tolerations, and pod affinity rules — all managed by the HyperShift Operator.

docs.title: Node Labels (what nodes announce)
docs.text:
# Request-serving nodes carry these labels:
hypershift.openshift.io/request-serving-component: "true"
hypershift.openshift.io/cluster: "ocm-prod-abc123"  # cluster-specific
topology.kubernetes.io/zone: "us-east-1a"            # AZ label

docs.title: Pod Anti-Affinity (what kube-apiserver pods require)
docs.text:
# kube-apiserver pods require:
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: hypershift.openshift.io/cluster
          operator: In
          values: ["ocm-prod-abc123"]
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
      # Ensure pods spread across 2 AZs

docs.title: Tolerations (what pods must have to schedule on tainted nodes)
docs.text:
tolerations:
- key: hypershift.openshift.io/request-serving-component
  value: "true"
  effect: NoSchedule

docs.title: Autoscaling: T-Shirt Transitions
docs.text:
When an HCP's memory usage crosses a size boundary, the cluster transitions to a larger t-shirt size:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> small: Cluster created (low load)
    small --> medium: Memory > 350MB sustained
    medium --> large: Memory > 1750MB sustained
    large --> extra_large: Memory > 3500MB sustained
    extra_large --> extra_extra_large: Memory > 7000MB sustained

    medium --> small: Memory < 300MB sustained (cooldown period)
    large --> medium: Memory < 1500MB sustained
    extra_large --> large: Memory < 3000MB sustained

A size transition triggers: 1. HyperShift Operator updates the node selector on kube-apiserver pods 2. New (larger) request-serving nodes are provisioned or claimed from placeholder pool 3. kube-apiserver pods migrate to larger nodes 4. Old smaller nodes are released and potentially terminated

docs.title: Troubleshooting Node Assignment
docs.text:
# Is the cluster assigned a size class?
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NS $CLUSTER_NAME \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.platform.aws.requestServingNodeType}'

# Are the right request-serving nodes available?
oc get nodes -l hypershift.openshift.io/cluster=$HC_NS \
  --show-labels

# Is a kube-apiserver pod pending?
oc get pods -n $HCP_NS -l app=kube-apiserver | grep Pending
oc describe pod -n $HCP_NS $PENDING_POD | grep -A 10 Events

# Is there a placeholder deficit?
oc get configmap -n hypershift-operator \
  -l hypershift.openshift.io/placeholder-size

Pods Pending on Scheduling

If kube-apiserver pods are Pending, the most common causes are: 1. No available request-serving nodes for this size class 2. AZ mismatch (anti-affinity can't be satisfied) 3. Taint not tolerated (pod config out of sync with node config) Start with oc describe pod → Events, then check node labels.

docs.title: Support Procedures
docs.text: Operational procedures for common customer-facing support scenarios: limited support, end-of-life handling, escalation, backups, and cluster configuration changes.

docs.title: Limited Support
docs.text: Limited support restricts what engineering teams are obligated to fix, while preserving the customer's ability to use their cluster. It's used when the customer has violated a support condition (e.g., non-standard configuration, unpaid subscription).

docs.title: Limited Support Lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant SRE
    participant osdctl
    participant OCM
    participant Alerts

    SRE->>osdctl: cluster support post
    osdctl->>OCM: POST /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/support_exceptions
    OCM-->>osdctl: OK (limited support active)
    Note right of OCM: Alert suppression label<br>added to HostedCluster
    OCM-->>Alerts: Silence all [HCP] alerts for cluster
    Note over SRE,Alerts: Customer can still use cluster<br>but SRE is not alerted

    SRE->>osdctl: cluster support delete
    osdctl->>OCM: DELETE support exception
    OCM-->>Alerts: Restore alert routing

docs.title: osdctl Commands
docs.text:
# Post limited support
osdctl cluster support post $CLUSTER_ID \
  --reason "L<reason-code>" \
  --note "Customer has modified managed resources in violation of support policy. OHSS-XXXX"

# Check current limited support status
osdctl cluster support status $CLUSTER_ID

# Delete limited support (restore full support)
osdctl cluster support delete $CLUSTER_ID

Use status not list

The correct subcommand is status, not list. osdctl cluster support list does not exist.

docs.title: Alert Suppression (Manual)
docs.text:
For temporary alert suppression without full limited support status:

# Add suppression label to HostedCluster
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID --service
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  -n $MC_NAMESPACE label manifestwork $CLUSTER_ID \
  "hypershift.openshift.io/suppress-alerts=true"

docs.title: End-of-Support Handling
docs.text: When a cluster reaches an unsupported version, SRE must initiate an upgrade.

docs.title: Process A: EUS Transition (Even y-streams → Extended Update Support)
docs.text:
For clusters running an even y-stream (e.g., 4.16, 4.18) where an EUS→EUS upgrade path exists:

# Transition the cluster to its EUS path
osdctl hcp transition-to-eus --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID

# What this does:
# 1. Verifies the cluster is on an eligible even y-stream
# 2. Configures the upgrade policy for the EUS channel
# 3. Schedules the upgrade via OCM

docs.title: Process B: Force Upgrade (Odd y-streams → next y-stream)
docs.text:
For clusters running an odd y-stream (e.g., 4.15, 4.17) that have no EUS path:

# Force-upgrade to the next supported version
osdctl hcp force-upgrade --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID --target-version 4.18.x

# What this does:
# 1. Creates an upgrade policy bypassing customer consent
# 2. Logs the action with the OHSS ticket
# 3. Triggers the upgrade immediately

Which Process?

Current Version Strategy 4.12, 4.14, 4.16, 4.18 (even) Process A: transition-to-eus 4.13, 4.15, 4.17, 4.19 (odd) Process B: force-upgrade

docs.title: Pre-EOS Communication
docs.text: Before forcing an upgrade, always: 1. Confirm the cluster ID and current version 2. Open an OHSS ticket for tracking 3. Check for customer open cases (may be aware and working on it) 4. Send customer notification (templates in Confluence)

docs.title: Backup Enable/Disable
docs.text:
OADP/Velero backups can be enabled or disabled per-cluster. Backups are enabled by default for all ROSA HCP clusters.

# Check current backup configuration
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID --manager
oc get backupstoragelocation -n openshift-adp

# Check backup schedule
oc get schedule -n openshift-adp | grep $CLUSTER_ID

# Disable backups (for a cluster that is being deleted)
# 1. Remove the DR ManifestWork (step 2 only, NEVER step 1)
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID --service
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  delete manifestwork ${CLUSTER_ID}-01-dr -n $MC_NAMESPACE

# Enable backups (re-create from OSDFM template)
# This is done automatically by OSDFM when a cluster is created
# For manual re-enable, contact the OSDFM team

Never delete -00-dr first

Always check the order: -01-dr (DR credentials) can be deleted and recreated. If you delete -00-dr (BackupStorageLocation) first, Velero loses its storage config and cannot back up or restore.

docs.title: Canary Sector
docs.text:
The canary sector is a set of clusters upgraded first within each region to validate new versions before the full fleet upgrade.

# Check which clusters are in the canary sector
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters | \
  jq -r '.items[] | select(.sector == "canary") | [.id, .region.id, .status] | @tsv'

# Promote a non-canary cluster to canary (for testing)
ocm patch /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters/$MC_ID \
  --body='{"sector":"canary"}'

# Demote back to standard
ocm patch /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters/$MC_ID \
  --body='{"sector":"main"}'

docs.title: Replacing the Pull Secret
docs.text: The global pull secret is used by worker nodes to pull Red Hat images. Replacing it doesn't affect the control plane (which runs on the MC with the MC's pull secret).

docs.title: Customer-Initiated (ROSA CLI)
docs.text:
Customers can replace their own pull secret: 

# Customer command
rosa edit cluster -c $CLUSTER_NAME \
  --pull-secret '{"auths":{"cloud.openshift.com":{"auth":"...","email":"user@example.com"}}}'

docs.title: SRE-Initiated (Break-Glass)
docs.text:
If the pull secret is corrupted and the customer cannot rotate it:

# Get the current pull secret to confirm format
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID
oc get secret pull-secret -n openshift-config \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.\.dockerconfigjson}' | base64 -d | jq .

# Create new pull secret (from customer's supplied credentials)
NEW_SECRET='{"auths":{"cloud.openshift.com":{"auth":"<base64-creds>",...}}}'

ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  patch secret pull-secret -n openshift-config \
  --type merge \
  -p '{"data":{".dockerconfigjson":"'$(echo $NEW_SECRET | base64 -w0)'"}}'

# Verify MachineConfig propagation (workers will roll with new secret)
oc get mcp

docs.title: Shared VPC Clusters
docs.text: A Shared VPC cluster uses a VPC owned by an organization's "owner" AWS account, with subnets shared to a "consumer" AWS account where the cluster actually runs.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph Owner["VPC Owner Account"]
        VPC["VPC + Subnets\n(shared via RAM)"]
        PZ["Private Hosted Zones\n(Route53)"]
    end
    subgraph Consumer["Cluster Account"]
        CLUSTER["ROSA HCP Cluster\n(control plane + workers)"]
    end

    VPC -->|"RAM share"| CLUSTER
    PZ -->|"VPC association"| CLUSTER
    CLUSTER -->|"creates records in"| PZ

    style VPC fill:#e3f2fd,color:#0d47a1
    style CLUSTER fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b5e20
    style PZ fill:#ede7f6,color:#4a148c

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. VPC owner must share the subnets to the consumer account via AWS RAM (Resource Access Manager)
  2. VPC owner must grant the consumer's installer role permission to create Route53 records in the private hosted zone
  3. Consumer account creates the cluster using the shared subnet IDs
  4. The installer IAM role in the consumer account must have a cross-account trust policy

docs.title: Troubleshooting Shared VPC
docs.text:
# Check if subnet sharing is visible from consumer account
aws ec2 describe-subnets \
  --subnet-ids $SUBNET_ID \
  --query 'Subnets[].{SubnetId:SubnetId,OwnerId:OwnerId,SharedVpc:SharedVpc}'

# Check Route53 PHZ association from consumer account

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Practical troubleshooting procedures for ROSA HCP clusters — from gathering evidence to diagnosing specific failure modes.

docs.title: Must-Gather Collection
docs.text: The osdctl hcp must-gather command is the primary tool for collecting diagnostic data from an HCP cluster.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
export CLUSTER_ID="<cluster-id>"
export JIRA_TICKET="<OHSS-XXXXX>"

# Collect must-gather for the HCP cluster (default: hcp target)
osdctl hcp must-gather --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID --reason $JIRA_TICKET

# Collect from the service cluster (ManifestWorks, ACM state)
osdctl hcp must-gather --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID --target sc --reason $JIRA_TICKET

# Collect from the management cluster's ACM hub
osdctl hcp must-gather --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID --target sc_acm --reason $JIRA_TICKET

# Collect from the management cluster directly
osdctl hcp must-gather --cluster-id $CLUSTER_ID --target mc --reason $JIRA_TICKET

docs.title: What Each Target Collects
docs.text: Target Collects hcp (default) Control plane pod logs, HCP CRs, conditions sc ManifestWorks, SC-level operator state sc_acm ACM hub state (ManagedClusters, ACM operator) mc MC cluster-level resources (not HCP namespace)

docs.title: Analyzing with omc
docs.text:
# After collecting must-gather:
ls must-gather.local.*

# Use omc to analyze (like 'oc' but reads from must-gather directory)
omc use ./must-gather.local.TIMESTAMP/
omc get pods -n $HCP_NAMESPACE
omc logs -n $HCP_NAMESPACE <pod-name>

docs.title: Noisy Neighbor Mitigation
docs.text: A "noisy neighbor" occurs when one or more HCPs on an MC consume so much CPU/memory that other HCPs degrade.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
# Find the top CPU-consuming HCP namespaces on an MC
ocm backplane login $HCP_CLUSTER_ID --manager
oc adm top pods -A --sort-by=cpu | head -20

# Check which HCPs are on the noisy MC
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters | \
  jq -r '.items[] | select(.cluster_management_reference.cluster_id == "'$MC_ID'") | .managed_clusters[]?.id'

# Look for resource-intensive operations (large etcd DB, high API rate)
oc get hostedclusters -A -o json | \
  jq -r '.items[] | [.metadata.name, .status.etcd.dbSize, .status.conditions[]?.reason] | @tsv'

docs.title: Mitigation 1: Request Non-Serving Node Resize
docs.text: The standard fix for node-level pressure is to resize the non-serving (worker) nodes of the overwhelmed MC pair. See Node Operations.

docs.title: Mitigation 2: Isolate to a Dedicated MachinePool
docs.text:
Isolate the noisy HCP to a dedicated set of nodes using MachinePool labels/taints:

# Label the dedicated machinepool nodes
oc label node $NODE_NAME dedicated=tenant-A

# Add taint to prevent other HCPs from scheduling
oc taint node $NODE_NAME dedicated=tenant-A:NoSchedule

# Patch the HostedControlPlane to use the dedicated nodes
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  -n $HCP_NAMESPACE patch hostedcontrolplane $DOMAIN_PREFIX \
  --type=merge -p '{
    "spec": {
      "nodeSelector": {"dedicated": "tenant-A"},
      "tolerations": [{"key": "dedicated", "value": "tenant-A", "effect": "NoSchedule"}]
    }
  }'

docs.title: MC Worker EBS Snapshot
docs.text:
Before replacing a worker node or troubleshooting disk corruption, capture an EBS snapshot:

# Find the instance ID of the MC worker node
INSTANCE_ID=$(oc get node $NODE_NAME -o json | \
  jq -r '.spec.providerID | split("/") | last')

# Find the root EBS volume
ROOT_VOL=$(aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --instance-ids $INSTANCE_ID \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].BlockDeviceMappings[?DeviceName==`/dev/xvda`].Ebs.VolumeId' \
  --output text)

# Take snapshot
SNAPSHOT_ID=$(aws ec2 create-snapshot \
  --volume-id $ROOT_VOL \
  --description "pre-investigation snapshot of $NODE_NAME ($JIRA_TICKET)" \
  --tag-specifications "ResourceType=snapshot,Tags=[{Key=cluster,Value=$MC_CLUSTER_ID},{Key=node,Value=$NODE_NAME},{Key=ticket,Value=$JIRA_TICKET}]" \
  --query 'SnapshotId' --output text)

echo "Snapshot: $SNAPSHOT_ID"

# Wait for completion
aws ec2 wait snapshot-completed --snapshot-ids $SNAPSHOT_ID
echo "Snapshot complete"

docs.title: Port Forward Without Debug Handler
docs.text:
MC worker nodes don't have the backplane debug handler. Use a proxy pod to forward ports to pods in the HCP namespace:

# Create a proxy pod that can forward to the etcd service
cat <<EOF | ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: proxy-pod
  namespace: $HCP_NAMESPACE
spec:
  containers:
  - name: proxy
    image: registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi-minimal:latest
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    ports:
    - containerPort: 2379
EOF

# Wait for the pod to start
oc wait pod/proxy-pod -n $HCP_NAMESPACE --for=condition=Ready --timeout=60s

# Port-forward through the proxy pod
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  port-forward -n $HCP_NAMESPACE pod/proxy-pod 2379:2379 &

# Now local:2379 maps to the pod's port 2379
# You can redirect this to the etcd service from inside the pod:
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- \
  -n $HCP_NAMESPACE exec proxy-pod -- \
  sh -c "nc -l -p 2379 -e nc etcd-client 2379"

# Clean up when done
oc delete pod proxy-pod -n $HCP_NAMESPACE

docs.title: Method 1: SSH via Jumphost Bastion
docs.text:
For public HCP clusters (API endpoint is public):

# Find the customer's SSH key secret
oc get hostedcluster $CLUSTER_NAME -n $HC_NS \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.sshKey.name}'

# Get the worker node's private IP
oc get node $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}'

# In ROSA HCP, SSH access to worker nodes requires:
# 1. The customer's SSH key pair (specified at cluster creation)
# 2. Access to the customer's VPC (via PrivateLink or public bastions)
# Worker nodes do NOT have public IPs by default

docs.title: Method 2: Jumphost to Workers (osdctl)
docs.text:
# For private clusters, use osdctl's backplane-based jumphost
osdctl hcp worker-shell $CLUSTER_ID $NODE_NAME

# This establishes an SSH connection via:
# SRE laptop → backplane proxy → MC → PrivateLink → customer VPC → worker node

docs.title: Method 3: Privileged Debug Pod on MC
docs.text:
Run a privileged pod on the same MC node for host-level debugging:

# This requires the specific MC node that runs the worker
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID --manager

# Find which MC node is hosting the troubled worker's HCP pod
oc get pods -n $HCP_NAMESPACE -o wide | grep kube-apiserver

# Run a privileged debug pod on that MC node
ocm backplane elevate "$JIRA_TICKET" -- debug node/$MC_NODE_NAME

docs.title: Route53 Quota Issues
docs.text:
If clusters fail to create with Route53QuotaExceeded or DNS delegation failures:

# Check hosted zones in use
aws route53 list-hosted-zones | jq '.HostedZones | length'
# Default limit: 500 hosted zones per account

# Check records per zone
aws route53 list-resource-record-sets \
  --hosted-zone-id $ZONE_ID | jq '.ResourceRecordSets | length'
# Default limit: 10,000 records per zone

# Request quota increase (file SR with AWS Support)
aws service-quotas create-case \
  --service-code route53 \
  --quota-code L-4EA4796A \
  --desired-value 1000

docs.title: Transit Gateway + Route53 VPC Association
docs.text:
For PrivateLink and private DNS resolution across multiple VPCs/accounts:

# Associate a Route53 hosted zone with a VPC in another account
# (requires cross-account authorization)

# Step 1: Authorize the association (in the hosted zone's account)
aws route53 create-vpc-association-authorization \
  --hosted-zone-id $ZONE_ID \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=$CUSTOMER_VPC_ID

# Step 2: Associate (in the VPC's account)
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone \
  --hosted-zone-id $ZONE_ID \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=$CUSTOMER_VPC_ID

# Step 3: Delete the authorization (cleanup)
aws route53 delete-vpc-association-authorization \
  --hosted-zone-id $ZONE_ID \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=$CUSTOMER_VPC_ID

# Verify association
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id $ZONE_ID | \
  jq '.VPCs[] | select(.VPCId == "'$CUSTOMER_VPC_ID'")'

docs.title: Upgrade Architecture
docs.text: This page explains how ROSA HCP control plane upgrades propagate through the system layers — from customer request to control plane pod replacement — and how to verify or unblock a stuck upgrade.

docs.title: Upgrade Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CUST as Customer
    participant OCM as OCM / Clusters Service
    participant SC as Service Cluster
    participant ACM as ACM (ManifestWork)
    participant MC as Management Cluster
    participant HO as HyperShift Operator
    participant CPO as Control Plane Operator

    CUST->>OCM: rosa upgrade cluster --version 4.17.5
    OCM->>OCM: Create upgrade_policy record
    OCM->>OCM: Run pre-flight checks
    Note right of OCM: If checks fail, upgrade marked failed
    OCM->>SC: Patch ManifestWork with new release image
    Note right of SC: Upgrade status → started
    SC->>ACM: ManifestWork applied
    ACM->>MC: Patch HostedCluster.spec.release.image
    MC->>HO: HyperShift Operator detects release change
    HO->>MC: Propagate to HostedControlPlane.spec.releaseImage
    MC->>CPO: CPO detects HostedControlPlane change
    CPO->>MC: Begin rolling update of control plane pods
    Note over CPO,MC: kube-apiserver → etcd → operators
    CPO-->>MC: ControlPlaneUpgradeComplete

Once Started, Cannot Cancel

Once an upgrade is marked as started in OCM, it cannot be cancelled or moved to failed status via API call. The upgrade must complete or be manually recovered.

docs.text:
The upgrade flows through 3 checkpoints. Work backwards from the hosted cluster to find where a stuck upgrade is broken:

    HC["HostedCluster\n(on Management Cluster)"]
    HCP2["HostedControlPlane\n(on Management Cluster)"]
    PODS["Control Plane Pods\n(CPO updates)"]

    MW -->|"ACM reconciles"| HC
    HC -->|"HyperShift Operator"| HCP2
    HCP2 -->|"CPO rolling update"| PODS

    style HC fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b5e20
    style HCP2 fill:#fff3e0,color:#bf360c
    style PODS fill:#ede7f6,color:#4a148c

ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID --service

# Check if the new release image is in the ManifestWork

  | jq '.spec.workload.manifests[] | select(.kind=="HostedCluster") | .spec.release'

Contact @ocm-rosa-hcp-ic in #sd-rosa-hcp.

  get hostedcontrolplanes ${DOMAIN_PREFIX} -ojson \
  | jq -r '.spec.releaseImage'

oc adm release info quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@<sha> -ojson \
  | jq -r '.metadata.version'

docs.title: Fleet Upgrades (SC/MC)
docs.text:
Management and Service clusters themselves are upgraded by the Advanced Upgrade Service (AUS), which uses a sector-based progressive rollout approach.

graph LR
    subgraph Progression["Sector Progression"]
        S1["Sector 1\nCanary"]
        S2["Sector 2\nEarly Adopters"]
        S3["Sector 3\nMain Fleet Wave 1"]
        S4["Sector 4\nMain Fleet Wave 2"]

        S1 -->|"success gates"| S2
        S2 -->|"success gates"| S3
        S3 -->|"success gates"| S4
    end

    style S1 fill:#ffebee,color:#b71c1c
    style S2 fill:#fff3e0,color:#bf360c
    style S3 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#0d47a1
    style S4 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b5e20

Key concepts: - Version blocks: Regex patterns preventing upgrades to untested versions (e.g., ^4\.17\..* blocks all 4.17.x) - Version inheritance: Production clusters can only upgrade to versions already deployed in stage - AUS Dashboard: Cluster Upgrade Overview

docs.title: MC/SC Upgrade Failure (MCSCUpgradeFailureSOP)
docs.text:
To identify whether an upgrade failure is on an MC or SC:

# Is this cluster a Management Cluster?
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters \
  | jq -r '.items[] | select(.cluster_management_reference.cluster_id == "$INTERNAL_ID")'

# Is this cluster a Service Cluster?
ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/service_clusters \
  | jq -r '.items[] | select(.cluster_management_reference.cluster_id == "$INTERNAL_ID")'

Incident Required

If an upgrade failure is confirmed on an MC or SC, declare an incident immediately — both cluster types serve many HCPs and impact can be large.

Mirror jobs run on a schedule and on demand when a new version needs to be published. They pull from Red Hat registries (with internet access) and push into the ZE root ECR.

docs.title: Required VPC Endpoints
docs.text:
Zero egress clusters require specific AWS PrivateLink endpoints. Without these, the cluster cannot function:

Endpoint Type Required For com.amazonaws.REGION.sts Interface IAM/IRSA token exchange com.amazonaws.REGION.ecr.api Interface ECR API calls com.amazonaws.REGION.ecr.dkr Interface ECR container pulls com.amazonaws.REGION.s3 Gateway S3 access (RHCOS ignition, etcd backups)

S3 must be a Gateway endpoint

S3 uses a Gateway-type endpoint, not an Interface-type. A common misconfiguration is setting S3 as Interface, which breaks ignition delivery to workers.

docs.title: ECR Credential Refresh CronJob
docs.text:
ECR tokens expire every 12 hours. A CronJob in kube-system on each ZE cluster refreshes the pull secret:

# Check the CronJob is present and recent
oc get cronjob -n kube-system | grep ecr

# Check the last job run
oc get jobs -n kube-system | grep ecr

# Check the last job's logs
oc logs -n kube-system job/ecr-credentials-refresh-XXXXX

If the CronJob fails and the token expires, new nodes cannot pull images and MachineConfig rollouts stall.

docs.title: Insights Operator (Disabled by Design)
docs.text:
The Insights Operator is deliberately disabled on Zero Egress clusters because it requires outbound internet connectivity to console.redhat.com.

# Verify Insights Operator is disabled
oc get clusteroperator insights
# STATUS: Available, Progressing: False, Degraded: False
# Conditions should show "Disabled" in message

# Check the HostedCluster annotation
oc get hostedcluster $CLUSTER_NAME -n $HC_NS \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.hypershift\.openshift\.io/insights-operator}'

Do not attempt to enable Insights Operator on ZE clusters — it will CrashLoop without internet access.

docs.title: Accessing a Zero Egress Cluster
docs.text:
Because ZE clusters have no public endpoints, access requires backplane and PrivateLink:

# Login via backplane (uses PrivateLink/VPCE chain)
ocm backplane login $CLUSTER_ID

# Verify private connectivity
oc cluster-info

If backplane access fails: 1. Check that PrivateLink VPC endpoint exists and is available 2. Check Transit Gateway route table entries 3. Confirm the cluster's hostedcluster.status.kubeconfig is populated

docs.title: Image Pull Failures
docs.text:
# On the guest cluster
oc get pods -A | grep -E "ImagePull|ErrImagePull"

# Check which registry images are being pulled from
oc get pods -n NAMESPACE POD_NAME -o yaml | grep -i image

# Should be ECR endpoints (*.dkr.ecr.*.amazonaws.com), not quay.io

If pulling from quay.io: The imageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP) or ImageDigestMirrorSet is misconfigured. 

oc get imagecontentsourcepolicy
oc get imagedigestmirrorset

If ECR pull fails: 

# Check VPC endpoints exist
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=service-name,Values=*ecr*"

# Check ECR token is valid (less than 12h old)
oc get secret pull-secret -n openshift-config -o jsonpath='{.data.\.dockerconfigjson}' \
  | base64 -d | jq '.auths | keys'

docs.title: Mirroring Verification
docs.text:
# Check if an image exists in the ZE ECR
aws ecr describe-images \
  --registry-id 135808946024 \
  --repository-name openshift/release \
  --image-ids imageTag=4.17.5-x86_64

# List recently pushed tags
aws ecr describe-images \
  --registry-id 135808946024 \
  --repository-name openshift/release \
  --query 'sort_by(imageDetails, &imagePushedAt)[-5:].[imageTags[0],imagePushedAt]'

docs.title: Cluster Install Stuck at Workers
docs.text:
Workers can't pull images → MachineConfig can't complete → install stalls:

  1. Check VPC endpoint for ecr.dkr (Interface) — must be available
  2. Check VPC endpoint for s3 (Gateway) — must be in route table
  3. Check ECR cross-account replication completed: 
    aws ecr describe-images --registry-id $CHILD_ACCOUNT_ID --repository-name openshift/release
  4. Check CRI-O logs on a worker node (via SSM): 
    osdctl hcp worker-log $CLUSTER_ID $NODE_NAME
